text:
sophia: Quick sync — thinking about moving compaction/eviction responsibilities into the scheduler instead of leaving them entirely in the batcher. Pros/cons?
ben: I'd bias toward eviction in the batcher to keep the scheduler lightweight.
kyle: We observed fragmentation when batcher-only handled eviction — lots of small holes, longer scans, and weird latency tails.
sophia: Right. If the scheduler had a compacted view (or could trigger compaction) it could avoid scheduling work into low-density lanes.
ben: That implies the scheduler needs a richer signal (in-flight sizes, per-lane density). That increases surface area.
kyle: Minimal option: batcher publishes a small summary every 200ms: per-lane occupancy, avg payload size, free_slots. Example:```json
{ "lane": "low", "occupancy": 0.62, "avg_tokens": 128, "free_slots": 12 }
```
tara: Or keep eviction ownership with batcher and add a compact RPC the scheduler can call during low-util periods: `POST /batcher/compact?window=<id>&mode=async`. Scheduler triggers, batcher does the work.
sophia: That keeps clear ownership boundaries — scheduler requests, batcher executes. Also helpful for multi-host KV consistency (batcher retains placement invariants).
ben: Tradeoff: extra RPCs + potential compaction pauses. We'll need async compaction and throttling to avoid tail spikes.
kyle: Also: admission credits need to be resilient to compaction. If compaction frees slots we should refund credits back to scheduler quickly to reuse capacity.
sophia: Agreed. Wire sketch: metrics + RPC + refund report. Proto:```text
/metrics lane_occupancy -> {lane, occupancy, avg_tokens}
POST /compact?window=...&mode=async -> {accepted:true, job_id}
POST /credits/refund -> {amount:int, token:string}
```
tara: Rollout strategy: start with passive metrics only (no RPC), observe scheduling improvements, then enable on-demand compaction in canary.
infra-bot: deploy-started: batcher-v3 -> canary (10%) us-west at 11:20 UTC :rocket:
ben: We should also add a "shaping" signal from scheduler -> batcher to request coalescing instead of immediate compaction. Lower risk.
kyle: Shaping must be sticky for X ms and idempotent to avoid oscillation between shape/compact. Add hysteresis.
sophia: Action items: (1) prototype compact RPC handler in batcher (async + rate-limit), (2) add lightweight lane metrics export, (3) define credit refund wire format. I'll draft an RFC with those.
ben: +1. Please include worst-case compaction pause numbers in perf tests.
tara: I'll add perf jobs to the canary checklist and simulate high-slot churn.
sophia: Thanks — will post RFC draft tomorrow. :thumbsup:
